hook: Injectable implants spotted fentanyl overdose in rats and delivered naloxone in under 6 minutes

readout.label: Autonomous rescue time, fentanyl overdose in rats

summary: RES-Q pairs wearable sensors with needle-injectable autoinjectors that fire a jet of naloxone through scar tissue, with implants triggered by signals passed through the body. In rats, a wearable pulse sensor detected fentanyl overdose and set off rescue automatically. Swine tests covered only implant communication, and no human data exist.
title: A network of syringe-injectable bioelectronics for closed-loop therapeutic rescue
